paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the old system could not get you all the way to God, and Jesus can. The writer says the law "made nothing perfect," and then he says "a better hope is introduced, by which we draw near to God" (Hebrews 7:19). Priests under the law kept coming and going because death kept them from continuing in office (Hebrews 7:23). Jesus is a priest "forever in the order of Melchizedek" (Hebrews 7:17), and that's why this chapter is full of good news.

Now look at WHY that matters to you. Because Jesus lives forever, "He has a permanent priesthood" (Hebrews 7:24). The writer says He is "able to save completely those who draw near to God through Him, since He always lives to intercede for them" (Hebrews 7:25). Think about that, friend. Right now, today, you have somebody speaking up for you, and He never clocks out.

And the work is DONE. Other high priests had to offer sacrifices every day, but Jesus "sacrificed for sin once for all when He offered up Himself" (Hebrews 7:27). He is also the guarantee of a better covenant, sealed with an oath (Hebrews 7:21-22). So you don't draw near to God by being perfect enough, you draw near through the One who already is. Come on in, friend. The door is open, and I'll keep the ovens warm.
